So a brief update on my @fundex and my @FundedHive accounts.

Disclaimer: The trading matters are my fault not theirs my results are my results no interpretation necessary beyond that.

Fundedhive: +6%
Fundex: Breakeven

A bit discrepancy I know. Its self inflicted. I am using Ctrader web for fundedhive and mt5 for fundex. When I open a trade on one, I completely forget about the other and either chase an entry when i realize I forgot or just skip it completely and in this market skipping a trade is often a victory. No trading condition etc has determined the result, purely human error. 

The execution is great at both companies, trading is really trading. I am still head wobbling a bit about the trading costs at fundex but its not really a detriment to my trading.

One thing that has happened though is the fundex risk mechanism has kicked in. Overall, I like it - most prop traders who aren't just coinflip gambling should see more longevity in their evaluations with it. Initially it was annoying for two reasons:

1) It appeared out of no where, without some sort of notice
2) It happened when I had trades open and the margin call function really triggers my neurons when I am trading, it had me searching whether I did something or some issue happened.

A solution to this would be to email the user clearly upon triggering. Perhaps also limit the change to when the user is flat to avoid full blown panic. I still don't actually know what my leverage is, trial and error of "no money" errors lead me to figure out what positions I can take but no real clarity is there. I think with this feedback they will implement some sort of alert system as its just common sense. I put this down to growing pains as I understand the business and how sometimes good ideas take a moment to perfect.

With Fundedhive, the journey has been smoother by chance I suspect. Its the one I am missing trades on the most so the results are smoother. Nothing surprising yet. In the end both of these accounts are about the funded experience not the challenge really. 

Another thing that may be a hidden outcome generator is the way I am applying my stop loss. On Fundedhive, I am using the ctrader function to insert stop and TP by %. On metatrader I am click dragging to approximate values. On one trade I got stopped on EUR/USD on fundedhive and not on fundex because I dragged to a support level on fundex vs the rigid stop of fundedhive. But in most instances the extra spare change of loss has been negative to fundex. 

If the funded models hold up then I can say both companies run a decent program although I can see this "dynamic leverage" as a problem for many in the industry as it does soften the ability to yolo an account which is what most people are doing to their phase 1's. 

I'm not at a funded stage yet to play with the A/B mechanism however I have been developing the how-to side of it to benefit from the system overall and avoid having to pay out a lot of a-book losses. Whether it works or not can't say. I'm not a trader just a hobbyist. 

Am I recommending these companies? If you have spare money and are filled up on prop accounts - could be interesting ones to add to your arsenal, but make sure you understand the program, each phase and how the funded accounts work. Work on a strategy to utilize the funded accounts the best. My opinion is, ignore the on demand payout stuff if you are patient with getting yourself more DD the funded accounts could be fantastic if you have a nice edge.
